title: For its first thirteen months, there was no App Store at all.
description:
For its first thirteen months, there was no App Store at all. Steve Jobs's actual plan was that there never would be. At WWDC in 2007 he told developers to build web apps for Safari instead: 'There's no SDK that you need!'

An Apple board member who, according to Walter Isaacson's biography of Jobs, phoned him 'half a dozen times' to lobby for native third-party apps. Jobs kept shutting the conversation down.

on 17 October 2007. Jobs announced a real software development kit was coming the following March. It shipped on schedule, on 6 March 2008.

Native apps already live when the App Store opened on 10 July 2008, more than a year after the iPhone itself went on sale. Jobs called it 'the biggest launch of my career.'

It took a board member phoning him again and again to change his mind.

Sources:
- https://9to5mac.com/2011/10/21/jobs-original-vision-for-the-iphone-no-third-party-native-apps: quotes Steve Jobs's 2007 WWDC statement in full ('There's no SDK that you need!'), reports the Isaacson biography's account of board member Art Levinson phoning Jobs 'half a dozen times' to lobby for native apps and Jobs initially quashing the idea, and the 17 October 2007 open letter announcing an SDK for March 2008.
- https://appleinsider.com/articles/08/07/10/apples_app_store_launches_with_more_than_500_apps: contemporaneous report, published the day of the launch, confirming the App Store went live on 10 July 2008 with more than 500 native apps, over 125 of them (more than 25%) free, and Jobs's 'biggest launch of my career' quote.
